title: Where is the first peak?
text: To find where our new peak is, set that entire argument to zero: $$2\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)=0$$. Solve for $$x.$$

title: Zero product property
text: By the zero product property, the argument is zero if $$2=0$$ (not possible) or $$x-\frac{\pi}{2}=0$$, which means $$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$$.

title: Phase shift
text: The phase shift is $$\frac{\pi}{2}$$ to the right.

title: Compare graphs
text: Compare the graph of $$\cos(2x-\frac{\pi}{2})$$ in gold and $$\cos\left(2\left(x-\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\right)$$ in blue. \n Both cosine graphs have period $$\pi.$$ The blue graph, $$\cos(2x-\pi/2),$$ has a peak at $$x=\frac{\pi}{4}$$. The gold graph, $$\cos(2(x-\pi/2)),$$ has a peak at $$x=\frac{\pi}{2}$$.\n##figure2.gif##
